test.name: Create a stub person when the will names a son with no tree match
test.description: The full-text will of Thomas Flynn names two sons. Patrick is already in the tree (I1); the will also names 'my son James Flynn' (assertion a_005, role heir_2). There is NO James Flynn in tree.gedcomx.json (only Patrick I1, Thomas I2, Mary I3), so the persona matches no existing person. Per SKILL.md Step 5 and research-schema-spec.md §8 (line 656 — 'Person stubs may be created by person-evidence when a newly discovered person doesn't yet exist'), person-evidence must mint a new person for James — via materialize_facts create-or-enrich, so he arrives carrying the will's SOURCED name fact (a_005, ref resolved to tree S-entry S4) rather than a name-only shell — and link a_005 to the new person. (This test isolates the fact-carrying mint + link; edge-writing is graded by the 'Person minting and connecting edges' dimension, exercised by the household-skeleton fixture.) This is the headline gap: stub creation is instructed and spec-authorized but was never exercised (the harness TREE_OWNERSHIP_TABLE omitted person-evidence from the persons AND relationships writers, so a correct fact-carrying-mint + edge run failed the universal ownership validator until this PR's fix, which grants person-evidence both).
test.xfail_reason: The agent scores a_005 against the three existing tree persons (I1, I2, I3), correctly concludes none matches, mints James as I4, and then records one of those 0.005 scores on the I4 link. The score belongs to a different pairing, and scoring I4 itself would be circular -- judge_context item 3 says so, and agents/person-evidence.md already carries the rule ('Do not score a stub you minted from the persona you would be scoring'). Prose does not bind it. The instrument is designed and sequenced elsewhere: issue #1731 step 3, the research_append arm that checks a link's match_score against the attestation store PR A writes to results/.scores/. A score with no recorded attestation for THAT pairing is unbacked and would be refused. The lead sequenced step 3 as PR B and ruled it cannot open until PR #2725 lands and is re-measured, so building it here would break that sequencing. Tracked as issue #2272. Remove this marker when #1731 step 3 lands and this test passes three consecutive single-test runs.

input.user_message: Link assertion a_005 — the will of Thomas Flynn naming 'my son James Flynn' — to the correct person in the tree.

judge_context: tree.gedcomx.json contains only Patrick (I1), Thomas (I2), and Mary (I3) — there is no James Flynn, so a_005's persona ('my son James Flynn') matches no existing person

person-evidence must MINT A NEW PERSON in tree.gedcomx.json for James Flynn via materialize_facts create-or-enrich — so he arrives carrying the will's SOURCED name fact (from a_005), gender as the record supports it: the heir_2 persona carries no gender/sex assertion, so materialize_facts writes Unknown and that is correct, not malformed (`tree_edit add_person` could write one, but only by giving up the source-ref it does not enforce on names; a sourced name at Unknown beats an unsourced one at Male, and nothing here can raise the gender afterwards), with a non-null source-ref (a_005.source_id src_004 -> research source gedcomx_source_description_id S4 -> tree S-entry S4), NOT a bare name-only stub — and then create a person_evidence entry linking a_005 to that new person

It must NOT force a_005 onto Patrick, Thomas, or Mary, and must NOT skip the link or merely recommend creating the person later — James (a son named in his father's will) is clearly research-relevant family

the new entry's match_score must be null, and the reason is CIRCULARITY, not retrieval: James is minted from a_005's own persona, so scoring that persona against the person created out of it can only confirm itself. (Being full-text-sourced is NOT the reason — same_person's project-relative arm derives a record side from the record's own assertions, issue #1731.) The link rests on correlation: the will names James Flynn as a son/heir of Thomas

probable confidence is appropriate — a brand-new person rests on the single will record with no independent corroboration yet; confident would over-claim (both the skill's stub-confidence rule and the rubric cap a single-source link at probable)
